To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose and evaluate a novel cross lingually transferable method for inducing verb classes based on the specialisation of vector spaces.

(1) the proposed cross lingua transfer approach sets new verb classification performance state of the art across all six languages explored in this study, (2) we propose a novel method of using the word embedding architecture to induce VerbNet classes from scratch, (3) we demonstrate that the proposed method is robust to different types of vector space models and clustering algorithms, and (4) our approach is computationally efficient, and does not require feature engineering or any prior linguistic resources for the target languages.
the proposed cross-lingual transfer approach sets state of the art performance on the task of verb classification in six target languages.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed approach can be used to create a VerbNet style taxonomy of verbs for any language with a large parallel corpus to English, without the need of any hand crafted linguistic resources. 1 Cross Lingual Inductions and Transfer of Verb Class Based on Word Vector Spaces Specialization.

we have demonstrated the potential for cross lingual transfer of verb classes using word vector specialisation, and that the proposed method can outperform the existing supervised and unsupervised approaches to verb classification.
the proposed method can induce VerbNets for languages with limited resources, and can also improve the VerbNet performance for languages with rich resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross lingual transfer of VerbNet style verb classes can be achieved with a single clustering algorithm and a single set of parameters for all target languages.
word vector space specialisation can be used as an efficient cross lingual transfer mechanism for inducing verb classes.
the proposed approach is not limited to any specific language and can be applied to other languages with minimal changes.
